Label: Research Information Sheet Title of the Project: Exercise Motivations and Eating Behaviors UT Austin Investigator: Katherine Schaumberg PhD You are invited to be part of a research study. Your participation is voluntary and it is totally up to you to decide whether you want to participate. Even if you decide to be part of the study now, you may change your mind and stop at any time. If you agree to take part in this study, you will be asked to complete a series of online questionnaires, including demographics, medical and treatment history, alcohol and drug use, and height and weight. Examples include: “In the past 12 months, how often have you had 4 or more drinks containing alcohol in one day or how often have you consumed marijuana?”, and “Are you currently receiving medical or psychiatric/psychological treatment? (Therapy, Dietitian, General Doctor, etc).” You will be asked about your exercise and eating habits and motivations for these behaviors, as well as your thoughts and feelings related to exercise, body image, weight gain, self-esteem, mood, mental health, and self-worth. Examples of these questions include: “People would be surprised if they knew how little I ate”, “I notice when I get hungry”, “I stop exercising when I am fatigued”, “What is the least you have ever weighed since reaching your current height?”, “Have you had a definite fear that you might gain weight?”, “I did not like how my body looked.”, “I spend more than three hours a day thinking about healthy food.”, “If I have eaten too much, I will do more exercise.”, “I am terrified of gaining weight.”, “How dissatisfied have you been with your weight?”, “If I do not exercise I will be an uninteresting person.” and “Do you have any mental health diagnoses?” In addition, some questions examine how exercise may affect your relationships with others, including family members and/or partners. You will also be presented with hypothetical scenarios related to exercise, in which you will be asked to indicate whether you would continue exercising under different conditions (e.g., when sick). Examples include: “Concerns have arisen between me and my family and/or my partner about the amount of exercise I do.” and “You had a bad stomachache that persisted throughout the day, making it uncomfortable to exercise. In this scenario, do you believe you would still find a way to engage in exercise?” You may skip any questions that make you uncomfortable or that you do not wish to answer and you may stop at any time. We expect that this study will take about 1.5-2 hours. You will be receiving 2 course credits through SONA for your participation in this study. Please note that if you do not finish the study in completion, you will not be assigned the 2 credits through SONA. However, the researchers working on this study have been designated as confidential employees. No identifiable information will be collected (e.g., name, date of birth). All data will be kept in a secure location that is only accessible by study staff.
